question: Seema switched on an electric circuit and went away to drink some water. She came back after 2 minutes and noticed that the circuit had 2.5 A of current flowing through it. The net charge that had flown through the circuit is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**300 C**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• The formula to calculate the net charge (Q) that has flowed through the circuit is given by **Q = I * t**, where I is the current and t is the time.

• In this problem, the current (I) is given as **2.5 A** and the time (t) is given as **2 minutes**.

• Since the time is given in minutes, it needs to be converted to seconds. Therefore, 2 minutes = **2 * 60 = 120 seconds**.

• Now, using the formula Q = I * t, we get Q = **2.5 A * 120 seconds = 300 C**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Current (I)**

• Electric current is the flow of electric charge (usually carried by moving electrons) through a conductor.

• The SI unit of electric current is the ampere (A).

• Current is measured using an instrument called an ammeter.

• **Charge (Q)**

• Electric charge is a physical property of matter that causes it to experience a force when placed in an electromagnetic field.

• The SI unit of electric charge is the coulomb (C).

• One coulomb is equal to the charge of approximately 6.242 × 10¹⁸ electrons.

• **Time (t)**

• In electrical calculations, time is usually measured in seconds (s).

• It is important to ensure that time is always in the correct unit (seconds) before performing any calculations involving current and charge.
